4. Nida Model 480 Analog Multimeterrvalent

In this lesson you will first measure a circuit that is operating properly.
INTRODUCTIONM
After verifying normal operation the computer may insert a fault
You will measure the circuit again and determine if a fault exists and the type of fault.
Let's begin the lesson on JUNCTION DIODE TROUBLESHOOTING PRACTICE...........
LESSON MENU
. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
JUNCTION DIODE TS PRACTICE
The following experiments reinforce procedures used to troubleshoot diode circuits. You will compare normal operation with measured circuit values to determine if a fault exists.
EXPERIMENT
After taking voltage drop measurements turn off power to the PC position. Resistance measurements can then be made to isolate the fault to a specific component.f a fault exists.
Would you like to try another troubleshooting experiment? No
If you would like to try the troubleshooting experiments again, select Experiment from the objective menu.
1. Return the Test Console to the initial control settings.
Return all equipment to its proper storage area.
This completes the experiment on JUNCTION DIODE TROUBLESHOOTING PRACTICE..
1. Set the Test Console controls to the initial control settings..........
2. Set the Positive Supply Voltage to 12.
3. Carefully plug PC130-22A into the Test Console PC1 position.
SWITCH POSITIONS - Up = closed
Circuit A is operating properly. Measure circuit voltage drops to verify normal operation.
Is Circuit A operating properly?
Your measured values should be close to the values shown. If these values are not obtained, check with your instructor.
TRY AGAIN!
What fault is indicated by your measurements?
Compare normal indications to your measured values. Note the applied voltage is dropped across D1.
TRY AGAIN!
